cohort: Women with a large niche (residual myometrium <= 3 mm) who wished to conceive and were scheduled for laparoscopic niche resection.
finding: Laparoscopic niche resection significantly reduced niche volume, and while overall changes in vaginal microbiota were not significant, women with the largest niche volume reduction demonstrated a favorable microbiome shift, and a post-operative Lactobacillus crispatus-dominant microbiota was associated with the highest pregnancy rate.
